questions.scenario_question: A media company needs a model to tag and describe thousands of archive photos. A teammate suggests starting with a language-only model because the team knows it best. What should the lead recommend?
questions.hint: Check the input type before the familiarity.

options.text: Use any model at random, as all models read images the same way and differ only in price.
options.business_rationale: Models differ in supported modalities and quality.

options.text: Postpone the project until audio models improve, since archive photos are best handled together with sound.
options.business_rationale: Audio is unrelated to tagging photos.

options.text: Keep the language-only model and describe every photo in the prompt by hand, because the team knows it well.
options.business_rationale: Hand-describing thousands of photos defeats the purpose. A multimodal model reads them directly.

options.text: A model that supports image input, since familiarity gives a text-only model no such ability.
options.business_rationale: Modality fit is a hard requirement; the team can still use the familiar model for downstream text tasks.

questions.scenario_question: A startup's prototype of a legal-clause explainer uses its most capable model for every request and the monthly bill is alarming. User testing shows most requests are simple. What is the best next step?
questions.hint: Spend capability only where it matters.

options.text: Test a smaller or faster model on simple requests, measure quality, and keep the stronger one for hard cases.
options.business_rationale: Matching model capacity to request difficulty typically cuts cost with limited quality impact.

options.text: Switch everything to the cheapest model on the market without testing, since the bill is the main problem.
options.business_rationale: Untested switching risks quality failures on complex clauses. Cost optimisation still needs evidence.

options.text: Carry on as is, because cost should never influence model choice while the product is still finding users.
options.business_rationale: Cost sustainability is a legitimate business criterion for any scalable product.

options.text: Ask users to write shorter questions to save cost, which would shrink the number of tokens processed.
options.business_rationale: Burdening users is not a strategy and may reduce quality.

questions.scenario_question: A trading-support assistant must provide a draft explanation within one second while an analyst is on a call. A highly capable model typically takes six seconds. How should the team proceed?
questions.hint: Latency can be a hard constraint.

options.text: Drop the time requirement so that any model fits, as the analyst can always read the draft after the call.
options.business_rationale: Dropping a genuine requirement to fit a model inverts the process.

options.text: Treat latency as a requirement and evaluate faster models against the one-second target.
options.business_rationale: A better answer that arrives too late fails the use case.

options.text: Raise the temperature to make the model respond faster, because looser sampling shortens the generation.
options.business_rationale: Temperature does not change response time meaningfully.

options.text: Pick the most capable model and let the analyst wait, since a better draft is worth a few extra seconds.
options.business_rationale: The use case is time-bound. Waiting breaks the call workflow.

questions.scenario_question: A defence contractor must run a language model entirely inside its own secure environment and customise it deeply. Which selection logic is most consistent with these requirements?
questions.hint: Deployment control and customisation weigh heavily.

options.text: Any model at all, since the location where the model is deployed does not matter for the contractor's rules.
options.business_rationale: Where data is processed is central here.

options.text: Consider open-weight models hosted in its own environment, accepting duty for operations, safety and updates.
options.business_rationale: Control over hosting and customisation is the priority, and the organisation takes on the effort.

options.text: Avoid models altogether, on the grounds that serious security requirements mean no AI can ever be used.
options.business_rationale: Secure deployment is possible with proper architecture; avoiding AI is not required.

options.text: A public consumer chatbot, because it is the easiest to start and needs no infrastructure work from the contractor.
options.business_rationale: Public consumer services conflict with isolation requirements.

questions.scenario_question: An HR team wants an assistant to rewrite job descriptions in a friendlier tone. Which is the best first approach to model selection?
questions.hint: Start simple for a simple task.

options.text: Train a custom model on all HR documents before writing a single prompt, so the tone matches the company.
options.business_rationale: Custom training is heavy for a task prompts can often handle.

options.text: Use a speech recognition model on the existing text, because it is designed to handle written language.
options.business_rationale: Speech recognition converts audio to text; the input here is already text.

options.text: Buy a video generation model, since modern HR content is increasingly delivered as short clips.
options.business_rationale: Video generation does not match text rewriting.

options.text: Start with a capable general-purpose text model, test with prompts and examples, and escalate only if needed.
options.business_rationale: A text-rewriting task rarely needs custom training.

questions.scenario_question: A hospital group is choosing between two models for summarising radiology reports. Which set of evaluation criteria is most appropriate?
questions.hint: Define what 'good' means for this use case.

options.text: Only the vendor's marketing description and parameter count, which summarise how capable each model is.
options.business_rationale: Parameter count and marketing do not measure clinical quality.

options.text: Only how eloquent the summaries sound, since fluent writing is the best sign of understanding.
options.business_rationale: Eloquence can hide errors and omissions.

options.text: Clinician-reviewed accuracy and omission rates, privacy fit, latency, cost.
options.business_rationale: Domain-specific quality and risk criteria are measured with domain experts.

options.text: Only the speed of the response, since radiologists are busy and a quick summary is always more useful.
options.business_rationale: Speed matters, but a fast summary that omits findings is dangerous.

questions.scenario_question: An insurer has built its claims-summary tool around one specific model version. Months later the vendor announces that version will be retired. What should the AI leader have planned for?
questions.hint: Models evolve and are retired.

options.text: Model lifecycle management: regression tests, a migration plan, and no hard dependence on one version.
options.business_rationale: Planning for change reduces disruption when models update or retire.

options.text: Rewriting the tool in a different programming language, which would remove the dependence on the retired version.
options.business_rationale: Programming language is unrelated to model retirement.

options.text: Freezing the entire business until the model returns, so that customers are never served by a lesser tool.
options.business_rationale: A retirement is a managed change, not a reason to stop operations.

options.text: Nothing, because models are permanent once purchased and vendors maintain old versions indefinitely.
options.business_rationale: Models are versioned and eventually retired, so planning is needed.

questions.scenario_question: A European public agency wants to use a managed model service but requires that data be processed within specific regions. Which factor should be confirmed during selection?
questions.hint: Where is data processed and stored?

options.text: Regional availability and data-residency options for the service, plus the provider's data-handling commitments.
options.business_rationale: Location constraints are compliance requirements that gate the choice.

options.text: Whether the model has a catchy name, since memorable names make adoption easier among agency staff.
options.business_rationale: Names have nothing to do with residency.

options.text: Whether the model can generate poetry, since creative ability shows how sophisticated its language skills are.
options.business_rationale: Creative output has no bearing on residency obligations.

options.text: Nothing, since every region is identical for compliance purposes and data location is not regulated.
options.business_rationale: Regulations can depend on location, so regions matter.

questions.scenario_question: A retailer compares two options for an assistant: a managed service with per-use pricing, and a self-hosted open model. Finance only compares the per-token price. What is missing from the analysis?
questions.hint: Look at total cost of ownership.

options.text: Only the colour scheme of the user interface, which affects staff satisfaction and therefore overall cost.
options.business_rationale: Interface style is not a cost driver of this kind.

options.text: Nothing, because the per-token price already captures every cost of running either option over a year.
options.business_rationale: Hosting, staffing and governance are significant costs outside token pricing.

options.text: Total cost, including infrastructure, engineering, monitoring, security and maintenance.
options.business_rationale: Operating costs often dominate, especially when self-hosting.

options.text: Only the location of the vendor's headquarters, which determines the tax rate applied to each invoice.
options.business_rationale: Location may matter for contracts but is not a cost component by itself.

questions.scenario_question: A telecom operator worries about being locked into a single model provider. Which strategy best manages the risk while still moving forward?
questions.hint: Reduce switching costs without stalling.

options.text: Never use any provider until lock-in is impossible, since switching costs can never be fully removed.
options.business_rationale: Zero lock-in is unrealistic; waiting forfeits value.

options.text: Use a platform offering several models, keep prompts and evaluation sets portable, and design for swapping.
options.business_rationale: Abstraction and portability make switching cheaper.

options.text: Build a new foundation model to avoid every dependency, since owning the model removes provider risk.
options.business_rationale: Training your own model is a heavy and rarely justified response to lock-in.

options.text: Hard-code one provider's special features throughout the product to get the best results from them.
options.business_rationale: Deep coupling increases switching cost.

questions.scenario_question: A chief digital officer wants a single model family that handles text, images, audio and video inputs for different business teams. Which Google model family is described?
questions.hint: Think multimodal general-purpose family.

options.text: Veo, because it is a general text assistant.
options.business_rationale: Veo is for video generation, not for general text work.

options.text: Imagen, because it is the family for every kind of input and output.
options.business_rationale: Imagen is specialised for generating images from text, not for general multimodal understanding.

options.text: Gemma, because it is designed only for video production.
options.business_rationale: Gemma is a family of lightweight open models, not a video-production service.

options.text: Gemini, Google's multimodal model family covering text, images, audio and video.
options.business_rationale: Gemini is positioned as a general multimodal family, with different model sizes for different needs.

questions.scenario_question: An ad agency needs to create original campaign images from written briefs. Which Google model family is specifically aimed at this need?
questions.hint: Image generation from text.

options.text: Gemma, which is a speech-recognition product for call centres.
options.business_rationale: Gemma is a family of open language models, not a speech product.

options.text: Chirp, which is the name of Google's image generation model.
options.business_rationale: Chirp is associated with speech, not image generation.

options.text: Imagen, which generates images from text prompts.
options.business_rationale: It matches the text-to-image requirement, with brand review remaining the agency's job.

options.text: Veo, which targets generating video clips from text.
options.business_rationale: Veo may suit later video ads but the task here is still images.

questions.scenario_question: A streaming marketer wants to produce short promotional video clips from text descriptions of scenes. Which Google model family best fits?
questions.hint: Moving images, not stills.

options.text: Gemma, because it is Google's only video model.
options.business_rationale: Gemma is an open language model family, not a video generator.

options.text: Veo, a video generation model family.
options.business_rationale: It is aimed at generating video from prompts, subject to brand and rights review.

options.text: Imagen, because it produces finished video with sound by default.
options.business_rationale: Imagen focuses on still images.

options.text: Any text-only Gemini model, because text models create video natively.
options.business_rationale: A text-only model does not generate video. Video generation uses a dedicated model.

questions.scenario_question: A research institute wants a lightweight model it can download and run on its own hardware, adapting it to its field. Which Google family is designed with this openness in mind?
questions.hint: Open-weight and lightweight.

options.text: Veo, because it is distributed as downloadable weights that teams can tune.
options.business_rationale: Veo is a video generation offering, not the open language model family.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise, because it is an open-weight model.
options.business_rationale: Gemini Enterprise is a workplace offering, not an open-weight model.

options.text: Imagen, because it is meant for on-premise text classification.
options.business_rationale: Imagen generates images and is not positioned that way.

options.text: Gemma, a family of lightweight open models from Google.
options.business_rationale: Gemma lets teams run and adapt models themselves, taking on operational responsibility.

questions.scenario_question: A contact-centre leader reads that Gemini comes in different model variants. What is the practical meaning for her selection decision?
questions.hint: Variants trade capability against cost and speed.

options.text: Variants differ in capability, speed and cost, so she should match the variant to task complexity and volume.
options.business_rationale: Larger variants often reason better; smaller ones respond faster and cost less.

options.text: All variants perform identically and differ only in name, so she can choose whichever is cheapest.
options.business_rationale: Variants are designed with different trade-offs.

options.text: Variants differ only in which language they speak, so she should pick by customer language mix.
options.business_rationale: Variants differ in capability and efficiency, not primarily in language.

options.text: She must always choose the largest variant for any task, because bigger variants are never worse.
options.business_rationale: Larger is not always better for simple, high-volume work.

questions.scenario_question: A retailer lists four needs: a conversational shopping assistant that reads product photos and text; promotional images; short product videos; and an on-premise open model for internal experiments. Which mapping to Google model families is most accurate?
questions.hint: Pair each need with its natural family.

options.text: Assistant: Veo; images: Gemma; videos: Imagen; open on-premise experiments: Gemini.
options.business_rationale: This mapping mismatches every family.

options.text: Assistant: Gemini; images: Imagen; videos: Veo; open on-premise experiments: Gemma.
options.business_rationale: Each family is aimed at a distinct need.

options.text: Assistant: Gemma; images: Veo; videos: Gemini; open on-premise experiments: Imagen.
options.business_rationale: Several pairings are wrong; for example Veo is not for images.

options.text: Everything should use Imagen, since one family covers all four needs.
options.business_rationale: Imagen cannot serve conversational or video needs.

questions.scenario_question: A startup must decide between using Gemini through a managed service and self-hosting Gemma for a summarisation product. It has two engineers, limited MLOps skills and wants to launch in six weeks. Which choice is better supported by the facts?
questions.hint: Weigh time-to-market and operations burden.

options.text: Wait until a larger team has been hired, so the company can host and operate whichever model it prefers.
options.business_rationale: Delay forgoes learning and market opportunity.

options.text: Build a new foundation model tailored to summarisation, since a bespoke model would be best for the product.
options.business_rationale: Training a new model is impractical for two engineers in six weeks.

options.text: Use Gemini through a managed service to launch quickly, and revisit Gemma if control or cost needs change.
options.business_rationale: Small teams with short timelines benefit from managed access.

options.text: Self-host Gemma because open models are always cheaper overall once the engineers have set them up.
options.business_rationale: Self-hosting adds infrastructure and operational costs that can exceed managed usage fees at small scale.

questions.scenario_question: An insurer wants to extract details from scanned claim forms, photos of damage and recorded phone statements in one workflow. Why is a multimodal model attractive?
questions.hint: One model, several input types.

options.text: One model handling text, images and audio in a single workflow.
options.business_rationale: Fewer handoffs can simplify the architecture, though accuracy should still be tested.

options.text: It works only for documents written in English, which is why insurers prefer it for national portfolios.
options.business_rationale: Language coverage varies by model and should be tested; the claim is not accurate as stated.

options.text: It removes the need for any human review of claims, since a single model sees all of the evidence at once.
options.business_rationale: Multimodality widens inputs; it does not remove accountability for claim decisions.

options.text: It guarantees perfect extraction from handwritten forms, because multimodal models read handwriting flawlessly.
options.business_rationale: Handwriting and poor scans can still cause errors.

questions.scenario_question: A media firm asks if one general text model should be used to create finished marketing images, because 'AI is AI'. Which response best reflects how model families work?
questions.hint: Specialisation matters.

options.text: Any language model can create finished images equally well, since all models share the same core design.
options.business_rationale: Text-only models do not generate images.

options.text: Image models can write legal contracts as well as lawyers, because they are trained on much more data.
options.business_rationale: Image models are not designed for legal drafting.

options.text: The distinction is purely cosmetic and does not affect results, so the firm should pick by price.
options.business_rationale: The distinction affects capability, cost and quality.

options.text: Different model families are built for different outputs, so image generation suits an image-generation model.
options.business_rationale: Choosing by output type improves quality and avoids poor results.

questions.scenario_question: An agency uses Imagen to create stylised images of people for an ad campaign. Legal asks what to do before publishing. Which action is most appropriate?
questions.hint: Generated content still needs checks.

options.text: Review for bias, likeness and brand safety, check terms and follow disclosure rules.
options.business_rationale: Generated media carries reputational and legal risks that require review.

options.text: Avoid generating images of people forever, since no review process could make such images safe to publish.
options.business_rationale: Responsible use is possible with controls, so a permanent ban is not required.

options.text: Publish immediately, since AI images are automatically safe and cannot copy anybody's likeness or style.
options.business_rationale: Generated images can include unintended likenesses or stereotypes.

options.text: Remove the review step to save time, since the campaign deadline is tight and the agency is trusted.
options.business_rationale: Review is the control that catches issues before publication.

questions.scenario_question: A consultant says, 'We bought Gemini, so employees now have the Gemini Enterprise workplace assistant.' Why might this be an inaccurate statement?
questions.hint: A model and a product built with models are different things.

options.text: Gemini is available only to consumers and never to businesses, so the consultant must be wrong about both.
options.business_rationale: Businesses can access Gemini models through business offerings.

options.text: Gemini is a family of models, whereas Gemini Enterprise is a separate workplace offering that uses such models.
options.business_rationale: Distinguishing the model from the product avoids buying the wrong thing.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise is an image model and not a workplace tool, so it cannot give employees an assistant.
options.business_rationale: That mischaracterises the offering.

options.text: The two names always refer to exactly the same product, so buying one means the company has the other.
options.business_rationale: They refer to different layers, a model family and a product.

questions.scenario_question: A bank's architecture board must approve 'the Google models' for use. A staff member proposes approving the whole brand in one decision. What is the stronger governance approach?
questions.hint: Risk is specific to model, task and data.

options.text: Ban all models until a perfect one exists, since any residual risk could harm customers or the bank's name.
options.business_rationale: Perfection is not a realistic standard.

options.text: Let each team decide privately without keeping records, so approvals are quick and local expertise is used.
options.business_rationale: Unrecorded decisions undermine oversight and auditability.

options.text: Approve the brand once and never revisit the decision, since a single review is cheaper and more consistent.
options.business_rationale: Models and uses change over time, so periodic review is needed.

options.text: Approve by use case and model, assessing risk, data sensitivity and controls.
options.business_rationale: Different models and uses create different risks, so approvals should be granular.

questions.scenario_question: A real-estate portal wants to (1) have an assistant read listing photos and describe features in text, and (2) separately produce staged-room images of empty apartments. Which statement about model types is most accurate?
questions.hint: Understanding images and creating images are different capabilities.

options.text: Only the first task needs AI, since a rules engine can create realistic staged-room images for the second.
options.business_rationale: A rules engine cannot create realistic staged images.

options.text: Neither task is possible without custom training, so the portal must first assemble its own large dataset.
options.business_rationale: Existing models support both kinds of tasks without custom training.

options.text: Reading photos to write descriptions is multimodal understanding, while staging rooms is image generation, possibly with different models.
options.business_rationale: Separating the capability needs helps pick the right model for each step.

options.text: Both tasks are identical, so a single text-to-image model solves both and the portal needs only one tool.
options.business_rationale: A text-to-image model creates images but is not the tool for describing existing photos.

questions.scenario_question: A political consultancy offers a campaign realistic AI-generated video of an opponent saying things they never said. What is the most appropriate leadership response?
questions.hint: Capability does not equal permission.

options.text: Accept if the video quality is high enough, since a convincing result shows the work was done to standard.
options.business_rationale: Quality makes deception more effective, not acceptable.

options.text: Decline: deceptive synthetic media harms trust and conflicts with responsible AI.
options.business_rationale: Responsible AI principles include avoiding deception and harm, regardless of technical capability.

options.text: Accept, because technically possible content is acceptable if the client pays and the work is legal somewhere.
options.business_rationale: Technical feasibility is not an ethical or legal standard.

options.text: Accept but remove the disclosure to avoid confusion, since viewers should judge the clips on their merits.
options.business_rationale: Removing disclosure increases deception.

questions.scenario_question: A new project manager asks which Google family to explore for a lightweight experiment where the team wants to inspect and modify the model locally. Which is the best answer?
questions.hint: Local, inspectable, adaptable.

options.text: Gemma, a lightweight open family suited to local experiments.
options.business_rationale: It offers the control the team wants.

options.text: Imagen, because it can be downloaded as a text editor and adapted for each of the team's projects.
options.business_rationale: Imagen is an image generation family, not a text editor.

options.text: Veo, because it is the lightweight open family the team can download and modify on its own hardware.
options.business_rationale: Veo is for video generation.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise, because it is a downloadable model that can be inspected and changed on a laptop.
options.business_rationale: It is a workplace offering rather than a downloadable model.

questions.scenario_question: A hotel chain wants to use Veo-generated promo clips showing its pools and rooms. Some of the generated scenes show amenities the hotel does not actually have. What is the key issue?
questions.hint: Generated content may depict things that are not true.

options.text: There is no issue, because the clips are AI-generated and viewers know promotional footage is idealised.
options.business_rationale: Misleading advertising rules apply regardless of how content was produced.

options.text: The only issue is video resolution, which can be raised before the clips go onto the website.
options.business_rationale: Quality is secondary to truthfulness.

options.text: Misrepresentation: generated visuals must be reviewed so marketing does not mislead guests about amenities.
options.business_rationale: Marketing claims must be accurate whatever tool produced the visuals.

options.text: The only issue is file size, which affects how quickly the clips load on guests' mobile phones.
options.business_rationale: File size is operational, not about accuracy.

questions.scenario_question: A CEO is told that the gen AI landscape has layers: infrastructure, models, platforms, agents and applications. She asks where an employee-facing assistant sits. What is the best answer?
questions.hint: Applications are what end users touch.

options.text: Inside the model's training dataset only, since the assistant is nothing more than the data it was shown.
options.business_rationale: Training data feeds a model but is not itself an assistant.

options.text: The infrastructure layer, because assistants are essentially specialised chips installed in company servers.
options.business_rationale: Infrastructure provides compute; assistants are higher-level software.

options.text: The data-centre cooling layer, since assistants depend on keeping the hardware at the right temperature.
options.business_rationale: Cooling is physical infrastructure and not where assistants live.

options.text: The application and agent layer, built on the models beneath it.
options.business_rationale: Employees interact with applications and agents; those rely on lower layers.

questions.scenario_question: A retailer wants gen AI in its store-operations app. Which layer decision best reflects a sensible balance of effort and differentiation?
questions.hint: Differentiate where it matters; consume where it is a commodity.

options.text: Buy a single tool and avoid integrating any retailer data, so that nothing sensitive reaches the model.
options.business_rationale: Without company data and workflow integration, differentiation is limited.

options.text: Consume infrastructure and models through a managed platform, and invest in the application and data that differentiate it.
options.business_rationale: Teams generally gain more by customising applications and data than by rebuilding commodity layers.

options.text: Avoid platforms and call the model manually for each request, so the team keeps full control of costs.
options.business_rationale: Manual processes do not scale and ignore platform benefits.

options.text: Build custom chips and a new foundation model first, so the retailer controls every layer from the start.
options.business_rationale: That is a huge investment rarely needed for a store-ops app.

questions.scenario_question: A company has three groups: employees wanting an assistant in everyday work, developers building a customer-facing app, and analysts needing document OCR. Which principle best guides which offerings to examine for each?
questions.hint: Different personas, different layers.

options.text: Match offerings to persona and need: ready-to-use tools for employees, a platform for developers, purpose-built services for tasks.
options.business_rationale: Different audiences call for different levels of abstraction.

options.text: Give all three groups one plain chat window with no integration, since every group asks questions of data.
options.business_rationale: A generic chat window lacks the integrations and controls each group needs.

options.text: Give all three groups the same developer platform, so the company supports and governs a single product.
options.business_rationale: Employees without development skills would struggle with a developer platform.

options.text: Defer all decisions until the groups agree on one model, because inconsistent tools confuse employees.
options.business_rationale: Needs differ; consensus on one model is not required.

questions.scenario_question: A telecom executive asks what 'inference' means in discussions about AI costs. What is the best explanation?
questions.hint: Using a trained model, as opposed to training it.

options.text: A particular type of data label that the data team adds to each example before training begins.
options.business_rationale: Labels are annotations; inference is model execution.

options.text: Writing the first training dataset for the model, which is the main cost of an AI project.
options.business_rationale: Dataset creation is separate from running the model.

options.text: The legal approval process that precedes a launch, whose duration drives much of the overall cost.
options.business_rationale: Legal approval is governance, not model execution.

options.text: Running a trained model to produce outputs for requests, which incurs ongoing cost with use.
options.business_rationale: Training happens up front; inference costs recur with usage.

questions.scenario_question: A logistics operator is considering an AI agent that reads shipment emails, checks a tracking system, and drafts customer updates. Where does the agent add value beyond a simple chat model?
questions.hint: Connecting reasoning to systems.

options.text: It removes the need for any tracking system, because the agent keeps the status of every shipment itself.
options.business_rationale: The agent depends on the tracking system as a source of truth.

options.text: It works only offline with no data connections, which makes it safer than a standard chat assistant.
options.business_rationale: Agents typically rely on connections to tools and data.

options.text: It can use tools and data sources to take multi-step actions instead of only generating text it is given.
options.business_rationale: Tool use and orchestration let the agent complete workflows.

options.text: It eliminates the need for governance, since an agent follows its instructions exactly and never errs.
options.business_rationale: Agents that act raise the need for governance, such as permissions and approval.

questions.scenario_question: A bank has several teams each experimenting with different gen AI tools, duplicating spending and creating inconsistent controls. What organisational response best fits the AI landscape?
questions.hint: Coordinate without blocking learning.

options.text: Shared standards, an approved catalogue and governance, with controlled experiments allowed.
options.business_rationale: A central framework reduces duplication and risk while preserving experimentation.

options.text: Centralise every decision in a single executive's inbox, so one person sees and approves every use.
options.business_rationale: A bottleneck slows progress and does not scale.

options.text: Ban all experimentation until a final architecture exists, which prevents any further duplicated spending.
options.business_rationale: That stalls learning; controlled experimentation should continue.

options.text: Let each team continue independently to maximise creativity, since central rules slow experimentation.
options.business_rationale: Fragmented tooling leads to inconsistent controls and wasted spending.

questions.scenario_question: A school district's IT director wants to know what separates 'using' a foundation model from 'training' one. Which is accurate?
questions.hint: Consumers versus builders of base models.

options.text: Every organisation must train its own foundation model to use AI, otherwise it will not own its results.
options.business_rationale: Training from scratch is expensive and rare.

options.text: Most organisations use existing foundation models via prompts, retrieval or light tuning, and few train one.
options.business_rationale: Using and adapting existing models is the common path.

options.text: Training and using a model cost about the same, since both processes involve the same amount of computing.
options.business_rationale: Training is vastly more costly than using.

options.text: Using a model means copying its weights onto the district's laptops, where staff can run it offline.
options.business_rationale: Most usage occurs through services, not weight copying.

questions.scenario_question: A pharma company's leaders compare a consumer chatbot with an enterprise-grade offering for internal use. Which attributes most differentiate enterprise offerings?
questions.hint: Controls, not cleverness.

options.text: A bigger free quota of casual jokes and chat features, which shows the product is more capable.
options.business_rationale: Entertainment features do not matter for enterprise readiness.

options.text: A promise from the vendor that it will never make errors in any answer it gives to employees.
options.business_rationale: No tool can promise zero errors.

options.text: A friendlier colour scheme and more playful design, which raise employee engagement with the tool.
options.business_rationale: Aesthetics do not make a tool enterprise-ready.

options.text: Security and access controls, governance commitments, auditability and administration.
options.business_rationale: Enterprise readiness is about control and governance as much as model quality.

questions.scenario_question: A professional-services firm discovers employees using personal AI accounts for client work. Which response is most effective over time?
questions.hint: People use unapproved tools when approved ones are missing.

options.text: Issue a ban and take no further action, since a firm rule is the clearest way to stop personal accounts.
options.business_rationale: Bans without alternatives push usage out of sight.

options.text: Ignore the behaviour since employees are productive, and client work is rarely confidential in practice.
options.business_rationale: Client confidentiality is at stake, so ignoring it creates liability.

options.text: Provide approved tools that meet real needs, with clear policy and training.
options.business_rationale: Giving a sanctioned, usable alternative reduces shadow AI.

options.text: Ask clients to stop sharing information with the firm, so that nothing sensitive can reach personal accounts.
options.business_rationale: That shifts responsibility and harms the relationship.

questions.scenario_question: A manufacturer's board wants to understand where gen AI typically creates business value. Which summary is most accurate?
questions.hint: Think of the main value categories.

options.text: Only marketing slogans and brand image, since customers rarely notice other effects of AI adoption.
options.business_rationale: Value extends well beyond marketing language.

options.text: Productivity, customer experience, faster content and knowledge access, and innovation, each needing measurement.
options.business_rationale: These are common value levers, to be validated by use case.

options.text: Only cost cutting through reduced headcount, since savings are the only value that appears in a budget.
options.business_rationale: Value includes growth, quality and speed as well as cost.

options.text: Value arrives automatically once the tool is switched on, so the board need not spend effort measuring it.
options.business_rationale: Value must be measured against baselines.

questions.scenario_question: Two banks use the same foundation model. One consistently achieves better results in customer service. Which factor most plausibly explains the difference?
questions.hint: What the model is given and how it is used.

options.text: The better bank employs more people titled 'prompt engineer', and job titles drive the quality of results.
options.business_rationale: Titles do not drive outcomes; practices do.

options.text: Luck alone explains it, since customer service results fluctuate randomly from one quarter to the next.
options.business_rationale: Systematic differences usually have causes in process and data.

options.text: The winning bank must have a secretly better model, even though both say they use the same foundation model.
options.business_rationale: They use the same model. The difference lies elsewhere.

options.text: Better use of proprietary data, workflow integration, evaluation and change management, not the model alone.
options.business_rationale: When models are widely available, differentiation lies in data and execution.

questions.scenario_question: A health-tech company buys a managed gen AI service and assumes the provider is responsible for everything about compliance. What concept is being overlooked?
questions.hint: Responsibility is split.

options.text: Providers take all legal liability for every customer use, so the company can rely on the contract alone.
options.business_rationale: Customers remain accountable for their own use cases and data.

options.text: Compliance ends once the contract is signed, because the provider keeps certifications up to date.
options.business_rationale: Compliance is ongoing.

options.text: Shared responsibility: the provider secures its platform, while the customer governs its configuration, use and data.
options.business_rationale: Customers keep accountability for their own use and data.

options.text: Compliance applies only to hardware, so a managed software service leaves the customer nothing to do.
options.business_rationale: Compliance spans data, processes and usage.

questions.scenario_question: A software firm's AI lead wants to launch a large, all-features assistant after a year of development. An advisor recommends a different path. Which is most consistent with good gen AI adoption?
questions.hint: Learn quickly with small bets.

options.text: Iterate: launch narrow pilots, measure, learn and expand, since capabilities and needs change quickly.
options.business_rationale: Short feedback loops reduce risk and focus investment.

options.text: Keep the year-long plan unchanged because plans should never change once the board has approved the budget.
options.business_rationale: Rigid plans fail in fast-moving fields.

options.text: Cancel the project because the field moves too fast for any single product to stay relevant for long.
options.business_rationale: Change is a reason to iterate, not to stop.

options.text: Launch with no measurement to move faster, since users will tell the team quickly if something is wrong.
options.business_rationale: Without measurement, learning and value are unknowable.

questions.scenario_question: A city official hears the term 'AI agent' and asks for a short definition suitable for a council briefing. Which is best?
questions.hint: Goal-directed software that acts.

options.text: Any spreadsheet containing formulas, since formulas decide what to compute without human intervention.
options.business_rationale: Formulas are fixed calculations, not goal-directed model behaviour.

options.text: Software that uses a model to pursue goals, choosing steps and tools within limits.
options.business_rationale: It emphasises both capability and the need for limits.

options.text: A static FAQ page that visitors consult to find answers to common questions about city services.
options.business_rationale: A static page cannot decide steps or use tools.

options.text: A human employee who uses AI at the office to complete tasks more quickly than their colleagues can.
options.business_rationale: An agent is software, not a person.

questions.scenario_question: An agribusiness uses a purpose-built vision API to detect plant disease from leaf photos, and considers switching to a general multimodal model. What is the most balanced view?
questions.hint: Specialised services can excel at narrow tasks.

options.text: Compare both on the company's images: a specialised service may be more accurate, cheaper or simpler for a narrow task.
options.business_rationale: Evidence on real data should decide.

options.text: Never evaluate alternatives once something works, because change adds risk without clear benefits.
options.business_rationale: Reviewing options periodically is wise as capabilities evolve.

options.text: Use both at random without measuring, so that the company gets a balanced view of their performance.
options.business_rationale: Random use yields no learning.

options.text: Always switch, since general models are better at everything and a single tool would simplify the stack.
options.business_rationale: General models are not always better on narrow tasks.

questions.scenario_question: A conglomerate's new Chief AI Officer must sequence the first year. Which order of activities is most defensible?
questions.hint: Foundations before scale.

options.text: Spend the year only on training a proprietary model, so the group owns its core technology outright.
options.business_rationale: That ignores near-term value and is rarely necessary.

options.text: Wait for regulations to finish evolving, so the group does not have to adapt its programme later.
options.business_rationale: Regulations will keep evolving; governance can proceed now.

options.text: Launch 50 pilots at once without governance, to show momentum and find the best ideas through volume.
options.business_rationale: Uncoordinated scale multiplies risk and cost.

options.text: Governance and data foundations, a few measurable pilots, then scale what works.
options.business_rationale: Sequencing manages risk and builds capability.

questions.scenario_question: A retailer rolls out an AI assistant but sees low adoption. Training was a single webinar. What is the most effective next step?
questions.hint: People need role-based support.

options.text: Cancel the rollout, since low adoption proves the retailer's staff have no real need for an assistant.
options.business_rationale: Low early adoption is addressable.

options.text: Mandate usage and monitor compliance only, since clear expectations are the quickest way to change habits.
options.business_rationale: Mandates without enablement breed resentment.

options.text: Role-based training on real workflows, with team champions and feedback.
options.business_rationale: Adoption depends on relevance and practice.

options.text: Replace the assistant with a bigger model, because people use tools more when the answers are better.
options.business_rationale: The issue is adoption, not necessarily capability.

questions.scenario_question: A 6,000-person engineering firm keeps project knowledge in wikis, shared drives and ticketing tools. New hires spend days hunting for answers. The CIO wants employees to ask questions in natural language and get answers drawn from those systems, respecting each person's existing access. Which offering is the most direct fit?
questions.hint: An employee-facing assistant that connects to company data, not a developer build.

options.text: A custom application assembled by the firm's developers on the agent platform, starting with model selection
options.business_rationale: That route is valid when requirements are unusual, but it adds build and maintenance effort when a ready workplace experience covers the need.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise, the workplace assistant and agent experience connected to company data sources
options.business_rationale: It serves employees directly, connects to internal systems and is designed to honour existing permissions.

options.text: A text-to-image model, so employees can visualise where project answers might be stored
options.business_rationale: Image generation does not retrieve answers from internal systems. It would suit creating diagrams or visuals.

options.text: A speech-to-text API connected to the wikis, so staff can dictate their questions to the system
options.business_rationale: Transcription converts audio to text but does not search or answer from company content on its own.

questions.scenario_question: A bank is piloting an employee assistant over internal documents. The security lead worries that a junior analyst could now surface board papers by asking the right question. Which design property should the team verify before launch?
questions.hint: AI should widen access to what people may see, not to what they may not.

options.text: That answers are limited to content each user is already permitted to access in the source systems
options.business_rationale: Permission-aware retrieval is what stops the assistant from becoming a side door into restricted material.

options.text: That the model has the largest context window available, which prevents it from revealing restricted content
options.business_rationale: Context size has no bearing on who may see what. Access control must be enforced on the data.

options.text: That the assistant has been given administrator rights so it can read every document and answer completely
options.business_rationale: Administrator-level reach is the opposite of least privilege and would expose restricted papers to anyone who asks.

options.text: That all documents are copied into a single public folder so the assistant has one place to search
options.business_rationale: Consolidating into a public location removes existing protections and creates the exposure the lead fears.

questions.scenario_question: A pharma company's staff already use a free consumer chatbot for drafting. The CISO wants a sanctioned alternative that connects to internal repositories, offers administration and audit controls, and keeps company data under enterprise terms. What best captures why a workplace offering such as Gemini Enterprise may suit this need?
questions.hint: Think controls, connectors and data terms, not just chat quality.

options.text: It lets each employee train a personal foundation model on their own laptop overnight
options.business_rationale: Personal model training is neither the purpose of a workplace assistant nor practical for most staff.

options.text: It removes the need for employees to review AI output, since enterprise tools are factually reliable
options.business_rationale: No enterprise tool guarantees accuracy. Review remains essential for regulated content.

options.text: It gives staff a smarter model than any consumer tool, so governance questions largely disappear
options.business_rationale: Model quality is only one factor. Governance depends on administration, data terms and controls.

options.text: It combines an AI assistant with company-data connections and enterprise administration and data-handling terms
options.business_rationale: Those controls address governance concerns that unmanaged consumer tools usually cannot.

questions.scenario_question: A finance operations manager wants non-developer analysts to create small agents that gather monthly figures from several internal tools and draft a variance summary, with a manager reviewing the result. Which approach is the best starting point?
questions.hint: Aim for configurable agents within the workplace experience, with oversight.

options.text: Use a video generation model to produce animated explanations of the variance each month
options.business_rationale: Video output does not gather figures from internal tools or produce a draft summary.

options.text: Commission a bespoke platform program for each agent, so developers write every integration from the beginning
options.business_rationale: Custom engineering suits complex needs but delays value on small, repetitive analyst tasks.

options.text: Use agent-building capabilities within the workplace offering, keeping a human approval step on outputs
options.business_rationale: Low-code agents let analysts automate routine gathering while review stays with the manager.

options.text: Let agents post variance summaries to the board automatically to save the review time
options.business_rationale: Removing review on financial reporting raises accuracy and accountability risk.

questions.scenario_question: An HR director wants all 2,000 employees to ask benefits and policy questions and get answers from the official handbook, without the company building any software. Which person-centred question should drive the offering choice?
questions.hint: Who uses it, and how much building is acceptable?

options.text: Does the handbook need to be converted into a video series by a generation model
options.business_rationale: That serves a different output goal, not question answering.

options.text: Will the company's data scientists be tuning a foundation model on benefits data this quarter
options.business_rationale: Model tuning is a separate, heavier path that the stated need does not require.

options.text: Does the company want to host an open model on its own hardware for the handbook
options.business_rationale: Self-hosting adds operations and expertise that a simple handbook Q&A does not call for.

options.text: Are the users employees who need a ready-to-use assistant over company content, with no development effort
options.business_rationale: Persona and build effort point to a workplace offering rather than a developer platform.

questions.scenario_question: Three months after rolling out a workplace assistant, a retailer sees strong sign-ups but few repeat users. Leaders propose buying a more capable model tier. Which action is most likely to improve sustained value?
questions.hint: Adoption problems are usually about fit and habit, not raw model power.

options.text: Pick high-value tasks per role, connect data, train, measure
options.business_rationale: Role-specific enablement and connected data make the assistant useful in daily work.

options.text: Replace the assistant with a spreadsheet template that staff fill in manually each week
options.business_rationale: That removes the capability rather than improving how it is used.

options.text: Upgrade to the most expensive model tier across the board and wait for people to notice the improvement
options.business_rationale: Spending more on capability does not address unclear use cases or missing data connections.

options.text: Restrict the assistant to a handful of power users so costs fall and complaints stop
options.business_rationale: Narrowing access may cut cost but gives up value and does nothing to build good usage habits.

questions.scenario_question: A manufacturer needs two things: (1) an assistant helping office staff find procedures and draft emails, and (2) a customer-facing mobile app feature that diagnoses a faulty machine from a photo and links to its own parts database. How should the offerings be matched?
questions.hint: One need is employee-facing and generic; the other is a custom product feature.

options.text: The workplace assistant for both, since an employee tool can be embedded in a customer app without changes
options.business_rationale: Customer-facing, branded features that integrate with a parts database generally need custom development.

options.text: A purpose-built translation API for both, since language is involved in each
options.business_rationale: Translation addresses only language conversion and neither stated need.

options.text: Workplace assistant for the first need; developer platform capabilities for the custom app feature
options.business_rationale: Each need is served at the layer that matches its audience and customisation level.

options.text: The developer platform for both, with office staff expected to write their own prompts in code
options.business_rationale: Office staff gain little from a developer-oriented build when a ready assistant already exists.

questions.scenario_question: A government agency is evaluating a workplace assistant. The records officer asks what to confirm about handling of prompts and outputs. Which question is the most useful in procurement?
questions.hint: Ask about retention, data use and auditability.

options.text: Whether the assistant's name is easy for citizens to remember when they call the helpdesk
options.business_rationale: Naming has no relation to records handling obligations.

options.text: How prompts, outputs and connected data are stored, retained, used and audited under the agreement
options.business_rationale: Those terms determine whether public-records and privacy obligations can be met.

options.text: Whether the tool can write poems on request during staff social events
options.business_rationale: Creative features do not address retention, privacy or audit requirements.

options.text: Whether the vendor promises that outputs will never contain mistakes, which removes review duties
options.business_rationale: No vendor can promise error-free output, and review duties remain with the agency.

questions.scenario_question: A consulting firm's analysts spend days assembling background research from public sources and internal notes. Leadership wants quicker first drafts while retaining accountability for facts shown to clients. What is the best way to frame the workplace AI capability?
questions.hint: Draft acceleration with human verification.

options.text: As a replacement for analysts, since the tool can compile and deliver client reports unaided
options.business_rationale: Unreviewed client deliverables carry professional liability and quality risk.

options.text: As a tool useful only for scheduling meetings, since research needs human intelligence alone
options.business_rationale: That underestimates drafting and synthesis help, which is well suited to AI with review.

options.text: A drafting aid whose sources analysts verify
options.business_rationale: It speeds first drafts while keeping accountable people responsible for accuracy.

options.text: As a database that is automatically correct because it quotes sources fluently
options.business_rationale: Fluent quoting does not guarantee that a source says what is claimed. Checking is still needed.

questions.scenario_question: A telecom company's sales team wants an assistant that can look up account history, summarise a customer's open issues and draft a follow-up email before each call. Which description best fits what a workplace agent can do?
questions.hint: Combines company data access, summarisation and drafting.

options.text: Pull system data, summarise, draft for the rep to review
options.business_rationale: That combines data connections, summarisation and drafting in one workflow, with the rep in control.

options.text: Replace the CRM so that account history is stored only inside the assistant's memory
options.business_rationale: An assistant is not a system of record, and relying on model memory for account data is unsafe.

options.text: Place outbound calls and agree contract changes with customers without any rep involvement
options.business_rationale: Fully autonomous commitments carry commercial and legal risk and are not the stated need.

options.text: Generate customer account histories from imagination whenever the CRM is slow to respond
options.business_rationale: Inventing history would be fabrication, which the workflow must prevent.

questions.scenario_question: A logistics firm piloted a workplace assistant with 200 dispatchers and measured a 12% drop in time-to-answer for routine procedure questions, but no change in on-time delivery. The CFO asks whether to scale. Which response is the most defensible?
questions.hint: Separate local efficiency from business outcome.

options.text: Claim that on-time delivery improved, since faster answers must have helped somewhere
options.business_rationale: Unsupported claims erode trust, and the pilot showed no delivery change.

options.text: Scale where the time saving matters, keep measuring downstream outcomes, and avoid claiming delivery gains the pilot did not show
options.business_rationale: The pilot proves a task-level efficiency; broader benefits need their own evidence.

options.text: Extend the pilot indefinitely with the same 200 users and no new measures
options.business_rationale: Open-ended piloting without new questions delays learning and decisions.

options.text: Cancel the project, because any pilot that fails to move the headline metric has no value
options.business_rationale: A real task-level saving still has value, which scaling decisions can weigh against cost.

questions.scenario_question: A law firm's partners want a workplace assistant to answer questions over its document management system. IT notes the documents have inconsistent matter permissions, with some stored in unrestricted folders. What should happen before connecting the repository?
questions.hint: Fix the foundation before exposing it through AI.

options.text: Connect everything immediately and rely on the model to hide anything confidential
options.business_rationale: A model is not an access-control mechanism and may reveal content that permissions allow.

options.text: Move all matters to one open folder so the assistant has a consistent view
options.business_rationale: Opening everything removes client confidentiality boundaries and breaches duties.

options.text: Delete the older matters so there is less to protect
options.business_rationale: Deleting records may breach retention duties and removes valuable precedent material.

options.text: Clean up permissions and classify sensitive matters so retrieval honours accurate access rules
options.business_rationale: AI retrieval surfaces whatever access allows, so access settings need to be right first.

questions.scenario_question: A hotel group with staff in eight countries wants one workplace assistant to help employees work in their own language with global policy documents written in English. Which capability is most relevant when evaluating options?
questions.hint: Language reach of both input and output.

options.text: Maximum image resolution, because multilingual quality depends on picture clarity
options.business_rationale: Image resolution is unrelated to language quality.

options.text: Multilingual quality, tested on the group's own languages
options.business_rationale: Staff need answers in their languages from English sources, so coverage and quality in each language matter.

options.text: Whether the assistant refuses all non-English questions to keep answers consistent
options.business_rationale: Refusing languages defeats the goal and denies staff the help they need.

options.text: Video generation quality, because policies are best explained in animated clips
options.business_rationale: Video does not address cross-language question answering over documents.

questions.scenario_question: A new project manager at an energy company says, 'We need Gemini, so let's give everyone the app.' The architect explains that Gemini Enterprise is the right thing to evaluate for employees. What is the most precise distinction?
questions.hint: Model family versus workplace product.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise is an open-weight model that employees can download and run themselves
options.business_rationale: That describes open model families, not a workplace product.

options.text: Gemini Enterprise is an image generator reserved for the marketing department
options.business_rationale: It is a broader workplace offering, not only an image tool.

options.text: Both terms describe the same consumer chat app, so there is nothing to distinguish
options.business_rationale: They describe different layers; one is models, the other is a business product.

options.text: Gemini is the model family; Gemini Enterprise is the workplace offering that brings AI assistants and agents to employees
options.business_rationale: Naming the layer correctly prevents buying or requesting the wrong thing.

questions.scenario_question: An insurer lets employees build their own workplace agents. The risk manager discovers an agent that emails customers payment reminders using data it was never intended to access. Which governance measure would have been most effective?
questions.hint: Control who can build, what they can reach, and what they can send.

options.text: Banning all agents permanently, regardless of purpose or controls
options.business_rationale: A permanent ban gives up legitimate productivity benefits that controls can safely capture.

options.text: Allowing agents to act freely, since mistakes will be caught later by customers
options.business_rationale: Using customers to detect errors transfers risk and harms trust.

options.text: Role-based controls on agent creation, least-privilege data access and approval before external communications
options.business_rationale: Layered permissions and approvals limit the damage that self-built agents can do.

options.text: A company-wide message asking employees to build agents carefully
options.business_rationale: Guidance without technical controls rarely prevents inappropriate access or sending.

questions.scenario_question: A 40-person accounting firm runs everything on Google Workspace. Partners want faster meeting follow-ups, quicker email drafting and help summarising long document threads, with no new tools to learn. Which offering fits best?
questions.hint: AI inside the apps people already use.

options.text: Gemini in Google Workspace, inside the apps staff use
options.business_rationale: It adds help within familiar tools and needs minimal change management.

options.text: An open-weight model hosted on the firm's own servers for confidential work
options.business_rationale: Self-hosting would add infrastructure burden the firm is unlikely to want for basic productivity.

options.text: A purpose-built vision API to read the contents of each email attachment image
options.business_rationale: Vision APIs read images and do not draft emails or summarise threads.

options.text: A custom agent application built from scratch by contractors on a developer platform
options.business_rationale: Heavy for a small firm whose needs are everyday productivity inside existing apps.

questions.scenario_question: A consulting firm's team leads lose time writing meeting notes and action lists after client calls held in Google Meet. They want notes without extra apps, but client sensitivity requires clear rules on use. What is the best approach?
questions.hint: Use the built-in capability, with governance on when it may be used.

options.text: Ban note-taking support, since any AI use would breach client confidentiality
options.business_rationale: Controlled use under enterprise terms can be acceptable, so a blanket ban is unnecessary.

options.text: Record every call and paste transcripts into a public chatbot to find action items quickly
options.business_rationale: Public tools put sensitive client content outside enterprise protections.

options.text: Meet's built-in notes, with a usage and review policy
options.business_rationale: It saves effort within existing tools while governance covers client sensitivity.

options.text: Let the AI send the action list to clients directly without any human check
options.business_rationale: Unreviewed external communication risks errors and unwanted disclosure.

questions.scenario_question: A media company's staff need AI drafting inside Docs and Gmail. Separately, its editors want to ask questions across articles stored in several non-Google systems. Which pairing is most sensible?
questions.hint: In-app help versus cross-system answers.

options.text: A text-to-image model for both, since editors prefer visual summaries
options.business_rationale: Image generation answers neither need.

options.text: Gemini in Workspace for both, since it will automatically index every third-party system
options.business_rationale: In-app assistants are not a substitute for connecting and governing other repositories.

options.text: A speech API for both, since text is just transcribed speech
options.business_rationale: A speech API converts audio and does not draft documents or answer questions.

options.text: Gemini in Workspace for drafting inside Docs and Gmail; a workplace assistant connected to the other systems for cross-system questions
options.business_rationale: Different needs: in-app assistance versus search and answers across repositories.

questions.scenario_question: A store-operations manager with limited spreadsheet skills must analyse weekly sales across 80 stores in Sheets. She wants help structuring the data and writing formulas without learning advanced functions. Which statement best describes the value of AI help in this setting?
questions.hint: Lowers the skill barrier while keeping her responsible for correctness.

options.text: It makes spreadsheet checks unnecessary, since generated formulas are always correct
options.business_rationale: Generated formulas can contain errors and should be checked.

options.text: It suggests and explains formulas, but she verifies totals
options.business_rationale: AI assistance reduces effort while validation protects against wrong calculations.

options.text: It requires her to move all data into a new analytics platform before it can help
options.business_rationale: In-app help works where the data already is, so no migration is implied.

options.text: It only works for text documents and cannot support spreadsheets
options.business_rationale: AI assistance in spreadsheets exists to support exactly this kind of task.

questions.scenario_question: A private clinic's admin team wants to use AI drafting in email to reply to patient enquiries. The practice manager asks what to check first. Which question matters most?
questions.hint: Sensitive data and the terms under which AI processes it.

options.text: What data the AI features access and process, under what terms, and whether this meets patient-privacy obligations
options.business_rationale: Health information carries strict duties, so data handling terms come first.

options.text: Whether the AI can write in a warm tone that patients prefer
options.business_rationale: Tone matters for experience but does not address privacy duties.

options.text: Whether the clinic's logo appears on AI-generated drafts automatically
options.business_rationale: Branding is a cosmetic matter, not a compliance one.

options.text: Whether other clinics are already using it, since popularity proves compliance
options.business_rationale: Popularity is not evidence that a use satisfies privacy rules.

questions.scenario_question: A university lecturer wants to upload a set of course readings and ask questions whose answers are drawn only from those documents, with citations to the passages used. Which kind of tool fits this need best?
questions.hint: Source-grounded notebook experience.

options.text: A source-grounded notebook tool such as NotebookLM, which answers from the uploaded documents and cites them
options.business_rationale: It limits answers to provided material, which helps verification.

options.text: A purpose-built speech synthesis API that reads the documents out loud
options.business_rationale: Reading aloud is not question answering over the content.

options.text: A model with no access to the readings, since broad training data is enough for a course
options.business_rationale: Without the actual readings, answers would not be tied to the course material.

options.text: A general video generation model, which can summarise readings as moving images
options.business_rationale: Video generation does not answer questions from specific documents with citations.

questions.scenario_question: A nonprofit enabled Gemini in Workspace for 150 staff. After a month, only fundraisers use it regularly. The operations director wants more value without extra spend. What is the best next step?
questions.hint: Show others how it helps their tasks.

options.text: Switch off the feature for everyone except fundraisers to focus the investment
options.business_rationale: Cutting access removes the chance to spread value to other teams.

options.text: Mandate daily use and track logins as the success measure
options.business_rationale: Mandates measure activity, not value, and can breed resentment.

options.text: Short role-based sessions on real tasks
options.business_rationale: Practical, role-relevant examples drive adoption at little cost.

options.text: Buy a separate developer platform subscription for every department
options.business_rationale: More spend and complexity do not address unclear use cases.

questions.scenario_question: A bank wants AI to draft internal emails and summarise documents in Workspace, but also needs a customer-facing mortgage-advice assistant that applies the bank's own rules, calls its core systems and is auditable. Which approach is best?
questions.hint: Use ready tools for the generic need and custom build for the regulated, integrated one.

options.text: Neither, because a bank cannot use generative AI under any circumstances
options.business_rationale: Banks do use generative AI with controls, so a blanket exclusion is not accurate.

options.text: Workspace AI for both, since it can call core banking systems through its drafting features
options.business_rationale: Productivity features are not designed to be a governed customer-facing advisory product.

options.text: A custom build for both, so staff write internal emails through a bespoke interface
options.business_rationale: Building bespoke tools for routine drafting wastes effort when built-in help exists.

options.text: Workspace AI internally; a governed custom build for customers
options.business_rationale: The regulated, integrated product needs control and auditability beyond productivity features.

questions.scenario_question: A software company's engineering manager wants help for developers writing and reviewing code inside their editors, with suggestions that reflect the company's codebase. Which kind of offering fits best?
questions.hint: A coding assistant for developers.

options.text: A text-to-image model, so developers can draw architecture diagrams
options.business_rationale: Diagram images do not provide code assistance.

options.text: An AI coding assistant such as Gemini Code Assist, integrated into developer tools
options.business_rationale: It targets developer productivity inside the tools engineers already use.

options.text: A translation API to convert code into other human languages
options.business_rationale: Translation of human languages is not what developers need here.

options.text: A customer-engagement conversational agent, since it can answer in natural language
options.business_rationale: That is built for customer conversations rather than developer workflows.

questions.scenario_question: A marketing coordinator has two hours to turn a campaign brief into a first draft of a slide deck with suggested images. Which capability of workplace AI helps most?
questions.hint: First-draft generation inside the presentation tool.

options.text: Publishing the deck to customers automatically once AI finishes drafting
options.business_rationale: Skipping review risks brand and factual errors.

options.text: Replacing the brand guidelines, since AI knows the company's identity automatically
options.business_rationale: AI does not inherently know brand rules unless they are supplied and checked.

options.text: Generating draft slide content and visuals from the brief, which she then edits for brand and accuracy
options.business_rationale: AI accelerates first drafts, leaving her to refine and approve.

options.text: Predicting next quarter's campaign revenue with certainty from the brief alone
options.business_rationale: A brief cannot yield a certain revenue prediction.

questions.scenario_question: A school district plans to enable AI features for teachers but not for students under 13. The administrator asks what capability matters most when evaluating productivity AI. Which is it?
questions.hint: Admin control by group.

options.text: The ability to write in rhyming verse for classroom decoration
options.business_rationale: Creative styles do not address age-group restrictions.

options.text: Administrative controls to enable or restrict AI features for specific user groups
options.business_rationale: Policy compliance depends on being able to switch features on for some groups and off for others.

options.text: Automatic sharing of student chats with teachers without student awareness
options.business_rationale: Hidden sharing raises transparency and privacy concerns.

options.text: A larger context window for the AI, so age rules can be remembered
options.business_rationale: Context size does not enforce group restrictions.

questions.scenario_question: A law firm's partners ask whether AI features in their productivity suite use client documents to train models for other customers. What is the best response from the technology director?
questions.hint: Read the terms; do not assume.

options.text: Avoid answering until clients ask, since proactive explanation invites questions
options.business_rationale: Proactive clarity on data handling builds trust and meets duties of confidentiality.

options.text: Tell the partners that all content is used publicly to improve the model
options.business_rationale: That is an unsupported assertion that could wrongly block valuable use.

options.text: Assure the partners that nothing is ever shared, based on the general reputation of the provider
options.business_rationale: Reputation is not a contractual commitment and the director should check the actual terms.

options.text: Check data-use terms and settings, and document them
options.business_rationale: The answer is contractual and configuration-dependent, so verification and documentation are needed.

questions.scenario_question: A construction firm's finance director asks how to evaluate AI productivity features in the office suite. Which approach produces the most trustworthy ROI estimate?
questions.hint: Measure before and after on real tasks.

options.text: Time tasks with and without AI, compare quality
options.business_rationale: Task-level baselines make savings visible and credible.

options.text: Ask the vendor to confirm that the investment will pay back within a year
options.business_rationale: A vendor promise is not evidence from the firm's own work.

options.text: Count how many AI buttons employees click each day
options.business_rationale: Clicks show interaction, not value.

options.text: Multiply the number of employees by an assumed 10 hours saved per week from vendor slides
options.business_rationale: Vendor averages are assumptions, not measurements of this firm.

questions.scenario_question: A city office wants meeting captions and translation to help colleagues who speak different languages participate in video calls. Which feature category is relevant?
questions.hint: Language support inside meetings.

options.text: Live captions and translation in the meeting tool
options.business_rationale: They address the need directly within the existing collaboration platform.

options.text: A sales forecasting model attached to the meetings calendar
options.business_rationale: Forecasting does not address language barriers.

options.text: A code-completion assistant for developers
options.business_rationale: Code completion is unrelated to multilingual meetings.

options.text: Image generation features to draw sign-language illustrations
options.business_rationale: That does not provide real-time language support during calls.

questions.scenario_question: A product team at a media company wants to test several models, including Google's own, third-party options and open models, before deciding which to use for article summarisation. They do not want to sign separate contracts or build separate integrations for each trial. Which capability of the developer platform fits?
questions.hint: A catalog that offers many models in one place.

options.text: A speech-to-text API, since summaries are often spoken aloud on podcasts
options.business_rationale: Transcription does not let the team compare summarisation models.

options.text: A workplace assistant for employees, which would hide which model is actually used
options.business_rationale: A workplace assistant does not give the team model-level choice for a product feature.

options.text: Model Garden, which lets teams discover and use Google, third-party and open models through the platform
options.business_rationale: A single catalog speeds up comparisons without separate integrations for each model.

options.text: Agent Search, which indexes the company's articles so staff can search them
